skill.name: auth
skill.description: Guides implementation of authentication patterns for web applications, including JWTs, OAuth2, RBAC, MFA, secure middleware, and zero-trust checks.
skill.summary: Build authentication and access-control patterns with practical examples for web applications.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious execution, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or system reconnaissance in the skill file. The static alerts are mostly false positives from Markdown fences, example OAuth endpoints, and variable names. Several instructional snippets contain insecure auth patterns that should be fixed before publication.

remediation.issue: Audit logging can record authorization headers.
remediation.suggestion: Redact Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and case-insensitive secret keys before logging request data.

remediation.issue: OAuth2 state is accepted but not verified.
remediation.suggestion: Store the expected state server-side and compare it during code exchange; add PKCE for public clients.

remediation.issue: CSP example permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unsafe script directives and use nonces or hashes for trusted scripts.
Replace placeholders with real device enrollment, attestation, and deny-by-default behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Authorization Headers May Be Logged
semantic_findings.description: The audit middleware logs request headers and only redacts exact keys named password, token, secret, and key. Authorization and cookie headers can expose session tokens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds headers from request.headers and logs request_data. The redaction list does not include Authorization, Cookie, or case-insensitive header matching.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth2 State Is Not Verified During Token Exchange
semantic_findings.description: The OAuth2 token exchange methods accept a state parameter but never compare it with a stored expected value. This can allow CSRF or login session swapping.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both provider methods receive state but never read or validate it before exchanging the code. The surrounding OAuth flow has no visible state store.

semantic_findings.title: Content Security Policy Example Allows Unsafe Scripts
semantic_findings.description: The security middleware recommends script-src values with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. These directives weaken CSP and can increase XSS impact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CSP string explicitly includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in script-src. That is a well-known insecure CSP pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Zero-Trust Device Check Trusts Every Device
semantic_findings.description: The zero-trust example returns true from the device trust helper. Copying this placeholder would bypass device trust checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper used by access validation returns True unconditionally. A nearby comment labels it as a placeholder, but direct reuse would be unsafe.

content.value_statement: Authentication code is hard to design safely across frameworks. This skill provides reusable patterns for JWTs, OAuth2, RBAC, MFA, middleware, and zero-trust reviews.
actual_capabilities: Explains JWT access and refresh token handling with expiration, token IDs, and revocation placeholders.
Shows OAuth2 provider flows for Google and GitHub login.
Demonstrates RBAC role and permission checks for protected functions.
Outlines MFA setup with TOTP QR codes, backup codes, SMS, and email channels.
Provides middleware examples for headers, rate limits, audit logging, and zero-trust checks.
limitations: The examples are templates and need security review before production use.
It does not include complete database persistence or deployment wiring.
Provider credentials, secrets, and redirect URIs must be configured outside the skill.
Some included examples need hardening before direct reuse.

use_cases.title: Launch Secure Login
use_cases.description: Build a starting authentication layer with JWTs, refresh tokens, and password hashing.

use_cases.title: Add Social Sign-In
use_cases.description: Connect Google or GitHub OAuth2 flows while planning state validation and provider settings.

use_cases.title: Review Access Controls
use_cases.description: Compare RBAC, MFA, middleware, and zero-trust examples against a product security checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth skill to outline a secure login flow for a small web app. Include password hashing, access tokens, and refresh tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Add OAuth2 Login
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth skill to design Google and GitHub sign-in for my app. Include redirect handling, state validation, scopes, and token storage.

prompt_templates.title: Design Authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth skill to design RBAC for users, moderators, admins, and resource owners. Include permission checks and audit events.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authentication design with this skill. Identify missing controls for OAuth2 state validation, audit logging, CSP, MFA recovery, and zero-trust access.

output_examples.input: I need a secure login plan for a FastAPI app.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture with password hashing, short-lived access tokens, refresh token rotation, revocation storage, and secret management requirements.

output_examples.input: Review my OAuth2 social login design.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering redirect URI controls, state validation, PKCE, provider scopes, token storage, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Design RBAC and MFA for admin users.
output_examples.output: Role and permission guidance with admin MFA requirements, recovery-code handling, audit events, and middleware placement.

best_practices: Treat every snippet as a starting point and run a security review before production.
Store secrets in managed secret storage and rotate them on a defined schedule.
Validate OAuth2 state, redirects, scopes, and PKCE for every provider.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder trust checks that always approve devices or networks.
Do not log full request headers without redacting authorization and cookie values.
Do not weaken CSP with unsafe script directives in production.

faq.question: Does this skill execute authentication code?
faq.answer: No. It provides Markdown guidance and examples that users can adapt.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it production-ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples require validation, testing, storage integration, and security hardening.

faq.question: Does it cover OAuth2?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Google and GitHub examples, but state validation and PKCE need explicit implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with MFA?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers TOTP, backup codes, and delivery channels at a template level.

faq.question: What should I review first?
faq.answer: Review secret management, token rotation, OAuth2 state checks, audit logging, CSP, and zero-trust placeholders.
